rationale: Tests ability to apply knowledge of shotgun choking to forensic range estimation — a core clinical reasoning task in firearm wound analysis.
Evaluates understanding of medicolegal inference from ammunition type — distinguishing rifled versus smooth-bore projectile evidence is foundational to court testimony.
Directly tests the classic entrance-vs-exit wound distinction — the most examined FM forensic wound ballistics fact and a frequent court question.
Tests understanding of blast injury classification — a NMC competency that maps to FM14.11 and is distinct from gunshot wound pathology.
Tests ability to differentiate intracranial haematoma types by mechanism and clinical timeline — critical for court testimony on cause and time of injury.
Addresses the common misconception about coup-contre-coup injuries — a frequently misapplied forensic concept in blunt head trauma testimony.
Applies knowledge of pedestrian-vehicle impact sequence to reconstruct the mechanism of injury — a standard forensic task in road traffic death investigations.
Tests understanding of crush syndrome pathophysiology — a clinically important complication with medicolegal significance in prolonged entrapment cases.
